extracted.intended_audience: Researchers reporting health economic evaluations for peer-reviewed journals, and the peer reviewers and journal editors assessing them; also analysts planning studies and health technology assessment bodies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and reporting health economic evaluations so they are identifiable, interpretable, and useful for decision making; aimed at authors, peer reviewers, editors, analysts, and HTA bodies. Emphasizes a 28-item CHEERS 2022 checklist with recommendations, explanations, and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to CHEERS 2022 28‑item checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the new CHEERS 2022 28-item checklist when reporting economic evaluations; the Explanation and Elaboration Report presents recommendations, explanations, and examples for each item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the full CHEERS 2022 checklist to ensure completeness of reporting; the E&E document supplies item-level recommendations, explanations and examples to aid implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the evaluation identifiable
rubrics_metrics.description: Report sufficient identifying information so the health economic evaluation can be found and distinguished in the literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reporting clearly states which health interventions are being compared and the overall study identity (e.g., title/abstract details) so the evaluation is readily identifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe which interventions were compared and the context
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly report which health interventions (and comparators) were compared and in what context the comparison took place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit descriptions of interventions, comparators, setting, population, and contextual factors that affect generalizability and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent reporting of methods (how the evaluation was undertaken)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear, comprehensive description of the methods used to conduct the economic evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report analytic approach, perspective, time horizon, modelling methods if used, sources and measurement of costs and outcomes, assumptions, and handling of uncertainty so readers and reviewers can appraise validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear presentation of findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the evaluation results and what the findings were in a way that supports interpretation and use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present primary outcomes, cost and consequence estimates, incremental results, measures of uncertainty, and any sensitivity or scenario analyses that affect conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report other details that aid interpretation and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Include additional information beyond methods and results that helps readers and decision makers interpret and apply the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide information such as model structure diagrams, data sources, parameter values, justification of key choices, limitations, and implications for decision making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report stakeholder involvement, including patients and the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe stakeholder engagement in the study, including roles of patients and the public where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how stakeholders informed study design, choice of outcomes, model inputs, interpretation, or dissemination, reflecting the increased role of stakeholder involvement emphasized in CHEERS 2022.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure applicability across intervention types and contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Make reporting broadly applicable to any form of intervention intended to improve health, whether simple or complex, across contexts (healthcare, public health, education, social care).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame methods and reporting to allow assessment of transferability and relevance across different intervention types and settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support transparency for decision making and HTA use
rubrics_metrics.description: Report with a level of transparency that supports decision makers and health technology assessment bodies in their evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given the increasing emphasis on transparency in decision making, provide sufficient detail for HTA bodies to assess, reproduce, or adapt the evaluation for policy or reimbursement decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider reporting requirements during study planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan studies with awareness of reporting requirements so that necessary data and documentation are collected to meet CHEERS standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarity with the CHEERS reporting checklist is useful for analysts when designing and planning studies to ensure all items can be reported fully at study completion.
